rules.checksTitle: Data checks for the outcome analysis
rules.checksSub: Applied in this order; a case's first failed check is its exclusion reason
rules.methodTitle: How expected activity is worked out
rules.methodSub: Agreed on 29 Sep 2026; counted tranche by tranche since 1–3 Oct 2026
rules.method1: The targets come in tranches. Each tranche's follow-up starts the day it opened — or the day the learner's F2F batch ended, if later — plus a buffer ({{first}} days for the first tranche, {{later}} for later ones).
rules.method2: Follow-up to the report date is rounded down to a multiple of {{step}} days (the table runs to {{max}} days).
rules.method3: Expected activity = for each tranche, the adoptions it asked for × the forms each should have generated at that tranche's follow-up (table below), added up.
rules.method4: Activity done ÷ expected gives the percentage; adoption target met is adoptions ÷ targets.
rules.targetsDefault: (default steps — set them in Programme settings)
rules.tableTitle: Forms expected per adoption, by follow-up
rules.tableSub: Cumulative forms one adoption should have generated after N days of follow-up; this report's tranche follow-ups are highlighted
rules.tableDefault: Default table built from the LAP visit schedule — edit it to load the revised sheet
rules.tableSaved: Expected-forms table saved — every project now uses it.
rules.tableNote: Counts are cumulative, so they can only stay the same or rise as the follow-up lengthens. Protein counts apply to ANC adoptions for now; an ANC adoption's baby visits are not yet counted in this table.
rules.caseSub: Used for each learner's own cases, Learner Activities and the follow-up flags
rules.case1: In pregnancy: an antenatal and a protein check on the adoption day and every {{every}} days, until the birth — or, if no birth is entered, until the due date (LMP + {{days}} days).
rules.case2: From the baby's adoption (its first contact, whatever its age): growth checks by the table; breastfeeding assessments by the table, only for follow-up before {{bf}} days of age.
rules.case3: Complementary feeding by age — at {{ages}} days. Counselling starts from {{from}} days, but the first assessment is at {{first}}: feeding starts at 180 days and needs 15 days to take hold. A baby adopted after {{first}} days is assessed from the first visit.
rules.case4: Follow-up is counted to the report date, up to {{max}} days of age.
rules.case5: A Staff Nurse's hospital cases expect the ward visits in the Staff Nurse row.
rules.lapSub: On which day of follow-up each form falls due. The expected-forms table below counts these up to each 15-day step.
rules.lapNote: Days count from the adoption. A Staff Nurse's facility adoption expects {{gm}} growth checks and {{bf}} breastfeeding assessments. The cumulative chart counts these day by day: a tranche's adoptions are all expected the day its buffer ends, and their forms then fall due on these days.

levels.tipTarget: Adoptions made ÷ adoptions asked by the targets in force today. Above 100% means more mothers were adopted than asked.
levels.tip1: Level 1 — the ideal. If every learner had adopted exactly what each tranche asked, on the day its buffer ended, how many forms should they have filled by today? That comes to {{rol}} per learner and {{sn}} per Staff Nurse. Forms done ÷ that.
levels.tip2: Level 2 — the adoptions actually made. Whatever was asked, take the mothers each learner really adopted and ask how many forms those should have produced, counting each from its tranche's start (after the buffer) in 15-day steps. Forms done ÷ that.
levels.tip3: Level 3 — each case by its own dates. Every mother is counted from her own adoption day, and her baby from birth: a pregnant mother adopted late needs fewer antenatal visits; a baby born later starts its own visits. Forms done ÷ that.

glance.title: {{name}} at a glance
glance.intro: Health workers ("learners") are trained face to face, then each one "adopts" a few pregnant mothers and mothers of young babies and visits them on a fixed schedule, filling in a form at each visit. This page shows, in plain numbers, whether the mothers are being adopted, whether the visits are happening, and whether the babies are growing better.

glance.wordsTitle: The words the other pages use

learner.meaning: A health worker (Anganwadi worker, ASHA, ANM, Staff Nurse …) trained by NurtureHUB.

adoption.meaning: A learner taking a mother (and her baby) under their care and visiting her on schedule.

types.meaning: A mother adopted while pregnant · after birth with a baby under 5 months · with a baby 5 months or older.

tranche.meaning: A round of adoptions asked of each learner. Each round starts after a few days' grace (the buffer).

forms.meaning: What a learner fills at a visit: growth check, breastfeeding, complementary feeding, antenatal check, protein count.

levels.meaning: Three ways to count the visits that should have happened: for everything asked; for the mothers actually adopted; for each mother by her own dates.

dyad.meaning: One mother and her baby, counted together in the growth results.

visits.meaning: The baby's measurements at birth, at adoption and at the last visit.
